primitives.name: Greedy Shrinkage-Cost Ratio
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model Cost-sensitive greedy (Algorithm 1): maintain version space S; at each step ask the question maximizing the shrinkage-cost ratio Δ_i(S,π_S)/c_i, where shrinkage Δ_i(S,π) = Σ_j [π(S^j)/π(S)]·(Σ_{k≠j} π(S^k)) = π(S) - Σ_j π(S^j)2/π(S) (expected version-space mass eliminated).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S': 'version space (set of consistent hypotheses)', 'π': 'prior probability distribution over hypotheses', 'Δ_i(S, π)': 'expected shrinkage from query i (dimensionless)', 'c_i': 'cost of query i (dollars or time units)'}
primitives.assumptions: Finite hypothesis set with unique zero-error hypothesis; unambiguous questions; known π, questions, and costs; realizable setting.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When exact optimization is infeasible due to exponential search space (e.g., batch queries), ε-approximate greedy suffices.

layer2.mapping: The shrinkage-cost ratio directly maps to GSI's utility function for selecting informative labels, where Δ represents information gain and c denotes resource expenditure.
layer2.telemetry: Expected reduction in posterior entropy per dollar spent.

primitives.name: Epsilon-Approximate Greedy
primitives.verbatim_quote: ε-approximate greedy (Algorithm 2): when argmax over questions is infeasible (e.g., batch AL has a question per subset — exponentially many), accept any question within (1-ε) of the max shrinkage-cost ratio; costs only a 1/(1-ε) factor.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'ε': 'approximation tolerance (dimensionless)', 'T^ε': 'ε-approximate greedy tree', 'C^*': 'optimal cost (dollars)', 'C(T^ε, π)': 'cost of ε-greedy strategy (dollars)'}
primitives.assumptions: Same as base model, plus intractability of exact argmax over queries.
primitives.breakdown_regime: In high-dimensional or combinatorial query spaces such as batch active learning.

layer2.mapping: Enables scalable implementation of greedy acquisition in large-scale batch settings by relaxing optimality constraints.
layer2.telemetry: Relative loss in performance compared to optimal greedy, bounded by 1/(1-ε).

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of the paper is extending Dasgupta’s binary, unit-cost active learning framework to a general setting with k-ary questions, non-uniform costs, and priors. It defines shrinkage Δ_i(S, π) as the expected reduction in version space mass upon querying question i, computed via π(S) − Σ_j π(S^j)^2 / π(S). This quantity measures how much uncertainty is resolved by a query. The greedy policy selects the question maximizing Δ_i(S, π)/c_i, balancing information gain against cost. Theoretical guarantees include logarithmic approximation bounds: C(T^g, π) ≤ 12C* · ln(1/min_h π(h)), where C* is the optimal cost. For batch settings, ε-approximate greedy ensures near-optimal performance with a multiplicative penalty of 1/(1−ε). The paper also introduces rounding techniques to handle cost-dependent bounds, yielding C(T^g, π) ≤ O(C* · ln(n·c_max/c_min)). These results justify GSE’s value-per-dollar acquisition logic but assume perfect knowledge of π, questions, and costs—a strong realizability assumption. Failure modes arise from misestimating π or assuming deterministic cost structures. The paper uniquely handles both non-uniform costs and priors across multi-class settings, distinguishing it from prior work.
